name: Ramelius Resources Limited
executive_summary: Ramelius Resources is a mid-tier Australian gold producer that the quantitative screen rates as a **Strong Buy**, passing 11 of 22 value models across all four metric families (cheapness, quality, dividend, risk) with a composite score of 73% and sector-relative score of 71%. The investment case rests on a low-multiple profile (P/E 11.5, P/B 1.4, dividend yield 2.7%) backed by a sharp earnings and cash-flow inflection in secondary Yahoo accounts, plus an acquisitive growth strategy that has expanded the asset base (Spartan Resources completed July 2025; Edna May flagged June 2026). The key debate is whether current profitability and screen cheapness reflect durable operating leverage and successful M&A integration, or are largely a function of elevated gold prices and peak-cycle margins — with H1 FY2026 news citing record EBITDA margins alongside lower production. Primary ASX filing bodies are **not available** in the source library (10 indexed headlines, zero downloadable extracts), limiting verification of reserves, AISC, rehabilitation provisions, and statutory risk disclosures.
investment_thesis:
The screen’s Strong Buy rating is well supported on classical value criteria. Ramelius passes Graham Defensive and Enterprising screens, Earnings Yield, FCF Yield, Low P/E + High Yield, Magic Formula, Dreman Contrarian, Composite Value, Financial Health, Economic Moat, and Dividend Growth — an unusually broad sweep for a single name. Headline metrics align: P/E 11.5 (below 15), P/B 1.39 (below 1.5), current ratio 3.30 (well above 2.0), ROE 10.6%, and reported FCF of approximately A$411m on the screening snapshot. Data quality is high (19/20 metrics present; score 0.95), and the signal has been stable for four weeks with conviction at 55%.

For a value investor, the thesis is a **quality mid-tier gold producer trading at a cyclical discount**. Yahoo fallback data (see Financial Review) show revenue rising from A$604m (FY2022) to A$883m (FY2024) and net profit from A$12m to A$217m, with FY2024 free cash flow of A$332m against net debt effectively nil (A$11m capital-lease obligations). The balance sheet offers optionality for dividends, buybacks, and bolt-on M&A: news references an A$250m capital-return programme and share buyback (December 2025), consistent with the Dividend Growth screen pass and FY2024 dividends paid of A$17m.

Business quality, insofar as news coverage allows assessment, has improved operationally — quarter updates and earnings-call headlines cite record margins and guidance delivery — while strategy has shifted toward scale via M&A (Spartan integration; Edna May acquisition headlines). The value case does not require a growth re-rating; it requires earnings and FCF to hold well above the depressed FY2022–23 base. That appears plausible on the financial trend, though unverified against primary filings and vulnerable to gold-price normalisation.
financial_review:
**Primary filings:** `filings_index.json` records regime `asx_announcements` with 10 indexed items (1 labelled annual, 0 interim, 9 other) and **zero body extracts** under `filings/bodies/`. Refetch was attempted for all 10 entries; none yielded downloadable text. The sole `annual`-labelled item is an unrelated *ARIKA RESOURCES LIMITED NOTICE OF ANNUAL GENERAL MEETING* (21 Oct 2025) — not a Ramelius annual report. Indexed `other` headlines include Spartan acquisition completion (31 Jul 2025), March 2026 and June 2026 quarter updates, and Edna May acquisition (29 Jun 2026), but without bodies these cannot be cited numerically. **No interim (half-year) filing bodies are present.**

**All figures below are drawn from `financials_annual.json` (Yahoo Finance fallback).** Quarterly income in that file is empty. H1 FY2026 operational figures appear only in news headlines, not in filing bodies or Yahoo annuals.

Revenue grew 40% in FY2024; net income rose 252% year-on-year. FY2022 was distorted by A$24m asset impairments and heavy amortisation (A$136m), consistent with acquisition-related intangibles. Gross profit expanded from A$312m (FY2022) to A$495m (FY2024) on revenue of A$883m.

**Interim gap:** News (20 Feb 2026, Yahoo Finance) cites record H1 FY2026 EBITDA margins and a robust interim dividend despite lower gold production; Investing.com (28 Apr 2026) references a Q3 FY2026 earnings-call transcript noting record margins. None of these figures can be cited numerically from primary filing bodies. No FY2025 full-year annual report body is indexed.
risks_and_flags:
**Regulatory / disclosure gap.** With no ASX annual report, half-year results, or quarter-update body extracts available, this memo cannot assess going-concern language, contingent liabilities, environmental rehabilitation estimates, reserve life, AISC guidance, debt covenants, or auditor emphasis-of-matter paragraphs from primary documents. This is the single largest research limitation.

**Commodity cyclicality.** As a gold producer, earnings are highly levered to bullion price and A$/US$ exchange rate (AUD/USD ~0.70 per macro context). FY2024’s profit surge may embed peak-cycle assumptions; a gold correction would compress margins faster than the low P/E implies.

**M&A and integration risk.** Spartan Resources acquisition completed July 2025; Edna May acquisition headlines appeared June 2026 (~A$300m deal per Motley Fool coverage). Heavy intangible amortisation (A$148m in FY2024) and periodic impairments (FY2022: A$24m) indicate an acquisitive history. Integration execution, synergy delivery, and goodwill/intangible write-down risk cannot be assessed without statutory filings.

**Production vs price-driven margins.** H1 FY2026 earnings-call coverage flags lower gold production despite record EBITDA margins — suggesting margin is price-driven rather than volume-driven. Grade or throughput deterioration would weaken the earnings base independently of valuation multiples.

**Share dilution.** The ~32% increase in shares outstanding between FY2023 and FY2024 dilutes per-share value creation; further equity for pipeline projects or M&A could compress per-share metrics.

**Governance / provisions.** Long-term provisions of A$48m and deferred tax liabilities of A$124m warrant scrutiny for closure-cost adequacy. Pension/post-retirement obligations are modest in Yahoo data (A$1.8m combined) but unverified against statutory disclosures. No covenant or related-party language is available from filing bodies.

**Sentiment / technical.** Kalkine articles (e.g. 26 Jun 2026 exhaustion-pattern piece; July 2026 share-price weakness coverage) signal mixed market sentiment despite screen strength — relevant to timing, not fundamentals.

research_rationale: Secondary financials and broad screen passes support the Strong Buy cheapness/quality/dividend case, but absent primary ASX filing bodies, unverified post-FY2024 M&A integration, and production softness against record margins prevent full confirmation and warrant measured conviction.
